'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Kyiv offensive (2022)|Kyiv offensive]]
****[[Battle of Kyiv (2022)|Battle of Kyiv]]
*****Four people are injured by a series of [[Russian Air Force]] strikes on infrastructure in [[Kyiv]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2022/03/23/ukraine-war-live-russia-seizes-humanitarian-convoy-ukrainian-leaders-say?postid=1209749124 (Euronews)]
*****Russian journalist [[Oksana Baulina]] is killed in shelling in Kyiv's [[Podilskyi District]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-60855732 (BBC News)]
***[[Capture of Chernobyl]]
****A laboratory near the [[Chernobyl Exclusion Zone]] is [[Looting|looted]] and destroyed by [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian soldiers]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-03-23-22/h_3c49a52f5331b712e44b27654ee96dea (CNN)] 
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[March 2022 Somalia attacks]]
***Two [[Kenya]]n guards and a [[Somalia|Somali]] [[Somali Police Force|policeman]] are killed during a shooting attack by [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] gunmen at [[Mogadishu International Airport]]. Two of the attackers are also killed. Several more people are wounded. All [[domestic flight|domestic]] and [[international flight]]s at the airport are suspended. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/somali-forces-kill-two-gunmen-trying-enter-mogadishu-army-base-state-tv-says-2022-03-23/ (Reuters)]
***Two [[suicide bombing|suicide bombers]] blow themselves up targeting a vehicle carrying politician [[Amina Mohamed Abdi]] in [[Beledweyne]], killing her and 47 more people. At least 105 more are injured. [http://reuters.com/world/africa/death-toll-somalia-attack-that-killed-lawmaker-rises-15-state-tv-2022-03-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**A [[car bomb]]ing kills four people in [[Aden]], [[Yemen]], including a [[Brigadier General]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/senior-yemeni-military-leader-killed-explosion-aden-sources-2022-03-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Boycott of Russia and Belarus]]
***[[Sanofi]] suspends the delivery of non-essential drugs to [[Russia]] and [[Belarus]]. However, essential and life-changing medicines and [[vaccine]]s will still be delivered. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/sanofi-halts-new-spending-non-essential-drugs-russia-belarus-2022-03-23/ (Reuters)]
***[[Nestlé]] announces that it will suspend sales of non-essential items in Russia, following similar company [[Boycott of Russia and Belarus|boycotts to Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nestle-suspend-brands-russia-including-kitkat-nesquik-2022-03-23/ (Reuters)]
**[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] demands that countries that he deems "unfriendly" pay for deliveries of [[natural gas]] in [[Russian ruble|rubles]]. [https://www.bloombergquint.com/business/putin-wants-hostile-states-to-pay-rubles-for-gas-interfax-says (Bloomberg)]
**The [[Moscow Stock Exchange]] will reopen in a limited capacity on March 24, ending the almost month-long shutdown of the stock exchange's activities. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-23/russian-stock-trading-to-resume-after-record-market-shutdown?srnd=premium-europe (Bloomberg)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[Sergeant at Arms of the United States House of Representatives|House Sergeant at Arms]] [[William J. Walker]] and [[Attending Physician of the United States Congress|Capitol physician]] [[Brian P. Monahan]] announce that a phased reopening of the [[United States Capitol]] will begin next week after the Capitol was closed for 2 years due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/599379-officials-launch-phased-capitol-reopening-starting-next-week (''The Hill'')]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****[[Moderna]] says that it will ask the [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. FDA]] for approval of [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|their COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/23/us/politics/moderna-coronavirus-vaccine-young-children.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec]]
*****[[Quebec]] health officials approve a fourth dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for high-risk groups in order to prepare for the possibility of a sixth wave of [[COVID-19]] cases in [[Provinces and territories of Canada|the province]]. [https://globalnews.ca/news/8704085/quebec-covid19-boileau-update/amp/ (Global News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] lifts its remaining COVID-19 restrictions including mandatory [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] tests for [[COVID-19 vaccination in South Africa|vaccinated]] travellers as the number of COVID-19 cases continues to decline. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2022/3/23/s-africa-eases-covid-curbs-scraps-pcr-tests-for-jabbed-travelers (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[South Korea]] surpasses 10 million cases of COVID-19. [https://news.sky.com/story/south-korea-covid-19-cases-hit-10m-leaving-crematoriums-and-funeral-homes-struggling-to-cope-12573261 (Sky News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Russia]]
**[[Poland–Russia relations]]
***[[Poland]] expels 45 staff of the Russian [[embassy]] in [[Warsaw]] for "[[spying]] activities". [https://www.rp.pl/kraj/art35923331-polska-wydala-45-rosyjskich-dyplomatow-msz-agresja-na-ukraine-dowodzi-ze-rosja-to-panstwo-wrogie-wobec-polski (''Rzeczpospolita'')]
**[[Anatoly Chubais]], the special envoy of the [[Kremlin]] for ties with international organisations, resigns from his post and leaves Russia. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-reformer-chubais-leaves-post-putins-special-representative-source-2022-03-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Belarus–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Belarus]] expels most Ukrainian [[diplomat]]s, accusing Kyiv of interfering in Belarus's domestic affairs. Only five diplomats will remain at the embassy in [[Minsk]]. Belarus additionally orders the closure of the [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] consulate in [[Brest, Belarus|Brest]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/belarus-expels-majority-of-ukrainian-diplomats (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian Foreign Minister]] [[Hossein Amir-Abdollahian]] says that [[Iran]] and other world powers are closer to finalizing an agreement to revive the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|2015 nuclear deal]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-foreign-minister-says-nuclear-deal-closer-than-ever-2022-03-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**[[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Criminal charges in the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
***[[January 6 United States Capitol attack|Capitol riot]] suspect Evan Neumann has been granted asylum in [[Belarus]] "indefinitely". Neumann claimed that he faced "political persecution" in the [[United States]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-60843262 (BBC News)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**The [[Israel Border Police]] arrests 17 [[Palestinians]] whom it suspects of taking part in [[riot]]s last month. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/17-palestinians-arrested-for-alleged-rioting-near-jerusalem-last-month/ (''Times of Israel'')]
